name: Methimazole
summary: A thionamide that blocks thyroid hormone synthesis and is first-line medical therapy for Graves disease, with rare but serious toxicity.
mechanism: Inhibits thyroid peroxidase, blocking iodination and coupling of thyroglobulin tyrosines and therefore de novo thyroid hormone synthesis.
pharmacodynamics: Lowers circulating thyroid hormone only as stored colloid depletes; also has immunomodulatory effects in Graves disease.

pharmacokinetics.onset: Clinical euthyroidism in 2–4 weeks (blocks synthesis, not release)

dosing.adult: Graves disease: 15–30 mg/day once daily initially, then maintenance 5–15 mg/day

safety.pregnancy: Avoid in the first trimester when possible — PTU is preferred; methimazole is associated with aplasia cutis and embryopathy
safety.lactation: Use lowest effective dose; monitor infant thyroid function
contraindications: History of agranulocytosis or severe hypersensitivity to thionamides
warnings: Agranulocytosis — stop and check CBC for fever or sore throat
Rash and arthralgia can be dose-limiting
Teratogenic; use PTU in early pregnancy
safety.overdose: No specific antidote; supportive care; may worsen myelosuppression

indications: Toxic adenoma and toxic multinodular goiter
Preparation for radioactive iodine or surgery
clinicalPearls: Effect is delayed 2–4 weeks because existing stored hormone must be depleted — add beta-blockers for symptom control meanwhile.
Educate patients: unexplained fever or sore throat means stop the drug and check a blood count.
good: Once-daily oral therapy with high remission rates in Graves disease.
bad: First trimester of pregnancy (use PTU), agranulocytosis history, or hepatic disease.
